_comment: Analyst review written after inspecting each chart and the Kotak daily data (25 Nov 2026 close). Every figure is taken from the stored Kotak candles. Shown in the PDF as 'Analyst view'.
_regime: Analyst view: the tape is strong but stretched. NIFTY 50 closed 25,819 on 25 Nov, about 7% above its 50-day EMA (24,118) and 7.6% above its 200-day SMA (23,999), and INDIA VIX (17.67) rose 13.9% over five sessions. Breadth is healthy rather than euphoric (63% of the universe above its 50-day EMA, 54% above its 200-day SMA). The regime supports long ideas, but an index this far above its averages also raises the odds of a sharp, broad pullback inside a 1–3 week window. That is the main portfolio-level risk to both ideas below, and the reason position risk is capped at 1% each.
_sectors: Analyst view: leadership is concentrated in financials (financial services, PSU banks, private banks: 'Leading', +3.7 to +4.3 points vs NIFTY over 20 sessions), with realty and FMCG improving; IT is the clearest laggard (−11.8 points, 'Lagging'). The two ideas are deliberately not in the leading groups: after a 15–20% sector run, banks offer poor reward:risk at fresh entries, while TITAN (consumer durables, 'Improving', roughly in line with NIFTY) and HCLTECH (IT, 'Lagging', although Nifty IT itself is above its 50- and 200-day averages) are pullback entries inside intact trends.
_backtest_verdict: The scan is used here as a disciplined filter (liquidity, trend, structural stops and targets, event risk), not as a forecasting model: over three years its setups showed no edge before costs. Each idea therefore has to stand on its own chart and its own defined risk, and is sized so that being wrong costs 1% of capital.

TITAN.summary: Pullback buy in a post-results uptrend: after the 5 Nov results the stock re-rated from ~4,300 to 5,057, then retraced to the 4,524–4,590 shelf at the 50-day EMA and turned up on 23 Nov. Risk 4.1% to 4,493; targets at the November and August highs (4,969 / 5,165).
TITAN.thesis: TITAN broke out of a two-month decline after its Q2 FY27 results (5 Nov): the 6 Nov session rose to 5,014 on 41 lakh shares (5.6x average), the heaviest volume in the chart window, and the stock reached 5,057 on 11 Nov. The retracement that followed was sharp — 18 Nov fell 5.3% on 1.4x volume, a genuine warning — but it stopped at 4,524 on 20 Nov, on the 3–4 Nov breakout shelf (4,562 close on 3 Nov), and the 23 Nov session closed back at 4,680 with a strong close near the high. The idea is that the post-results demand defends that shelf and the stock re-tests the November supply. What argues against it: the 23 Nov close was still marginally below the 50-day EMA (4,700) and the 20-day EMA (4,724), so this is a reclaim attempt, not a confirmed resumption; a close below 4,524 would mean the results breakout has failed. The buy-stop above 4,686.70 triggered on 25 Nov (opened 4,694) — the stock then traded down to 4,611 and closed 4,686.60, so follow-through is still unproven.
TITAN.events_note: No board meeting or record date is announced inside the holding window. Q2 FY27 results were on 5 Nov 2026; Q3 results are expected around February 2027 (last year's Q3 board meeting was on 10 Feb 2026). Sources: company / exchange filings via web search, 25 Nov 2026.

HCLTECH.summary: Pullback buy above the 13 Oct results gap: the stock jumped 8.4% on 7.8x volume, ranged 1,364–1,469 for three weeks, retraced to 1,309 near the 50-day EMA and turned up on rising volume. Risk 5.6% to 1,300; T1 at the range top 1,467. Lower conviction: the 200-day SMA is still falling and IT lags NIFTY.
HCLTECH.thesis: HCLTECH re-rated on its Q2 FY27 results (board meeting 12 Oct): on 13 Oct it opened at 1,245 (1.8% above the 1,223 prior close) and closed at 1,326, up 8.4%, on 217 lakh shares (7.8x average). The stock then built a 1,364–1,469 range for three weeks, which is the supply T1 is set beneath. The pullback from 1,469 bottomed at 1,309 on 19 Nov, just under the 50-day EMA (1,346) but well above the 1,223–1,245 gap zone, and the next two sessions closed higher on 1.2x and 1.4x average volume. As long as the gap holds, the October re-rating is intact. This is the weaker of the two ideas and should be read that way: the 200-day SMA (1,300) is still declining after a year-long downtrend, Nifty IT is lagging the index over 20 sessions, and the stock's 20-session return trails NIFTY by ~14 points (relative strength scored 3/15). The stop at 1,300.30 sits below the 19 Nov low and the 200-day SMA; a break there would put the stock back into its longer-term downtrend. The buy-stop above 1,378 triggered on 25 Nov at the 1,390 open; the stock closed 1,380.
HCLTECH.events_note: No board meeting or dividend record date is announced inside the holding window. Q2 FY27 results board meeting was 12 Oct 2026; Q3 results and the usual interim dividend are expected in mid-January 2027 (last year's Q3 meeting was 12 Jan 2026), after the time stop. Sources: company / exchange filings via web search, 25 Nov 2026.

_limitations: Both ideas are long and both depend on the broad market not pulling back sharply; they are not independent bets, even though their 60-day return correlation passed the 0.75 cap.

Both ideas triggered on a gap at the 25 Nov open, so their paper entries (4,696.35 and 1,390.69) are worse than the planned triggers; reward:risk measured from the actual fills is lower than the published figures (TITAN 1.34 / 2.31, HCLTECH 0.84 / 1.62 to T1 / T2); HCLTECH's T1 now offers less than 1R from the actual fill.

Event checks for the final ideas were made by web search of company and exchange filings because the NSE website refuses scripted access from this machine and the browser extension was not connected; the exchange announcement pages should be re-checked before acting.
